name: Higgs boson event confidence interval estimation
description: The task is to estimate the confidence interval for the signal strength (µ), representing the number of Higgs boson events normalized by the Standard Model prediction, while accounting for systematic uncertainties in simulated proton-proton collision data.

cr:input.name: FAIR Universe HiggsML Uncertainty Dataset
cr:input.description: A tabular dataset containing 280 million rows, each representing a simulated proton-proton collision event with 28 features. Features include primary attributes such as energy and momentum of particles, derived attributes calculated using domain-specific knowledge, and a label indicating event type (e.g., Higgs boson or background).
cr:input.contentUrl: [FILL IN THE BLANK: dataset download URL]

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: The output consists of a 68.27% confidence interval for the signal strength (µ), represented as two bounds (µ16, µ84). µ values range from 0.1 to 3.

field.name: µ16
field.description: Lower bound of the 68.27% confidence interval for the signal strength (µ). Example: 0.8.

field.name: µ84
field.description: Upper bound of the 68.27% confidence interval for the signal strength (µ). Example: 1.2.

cr:evaluation.notes: The Quantile Score is calculated as -ln((w + ϵ)f(c)), where w is the average interval width, c is the coverage, and f(c) is a penalizing function for deviations from 68.27% coverage. Overestimating uncertainty incurs a smaller penalty than underestimating it.
